title: Troubleshooting Services and Networking; Monitoring Resource Usage

header.html: Troubleshoot services and networking; Monitor cluster and application resource usage
Kubernetes v1.37.0, Metrics Server v0.9.0 (installed from its release manifest with --kubelet-insecure-tls, needed only because the lab nodes use self-signed kubelet certificates)

html:
1Service troubleshooting: walk the path

A request travels: client Pod -> DNS name -> Service ClusterIP -> kube-proxy rules -> ready Pod IP -> container port. Test each hop; the first one that fails is the problem.

Step Test If it fails
1. Name resolves k exec client -- nslookup web.net4 DNS problem (CoreDNS, Pod DNS policy): section 3
2. Service exists, right port k get svc web -o wide; k describe svc web wrong namespace or name; port mismatch
3. Service has endpoints k get endpointslices -l kubernetes.io/service-name=web empty: selector typo or Pods not Ready
4. Pods Ready k get pods --show-labels readiness probe failing, crash loop
5. targetPort matches the container k describe svc web, container port "connection refused": wrong targetPort
6. Policy blocks it k get netpol -A timeout (Module 9)
7. Reaches the Pod directly k exec client -- wget -qO- -T3 http://<podIP> works but Service does not: Service config; fails: Pod or policy

Symptom to cause table:

Symptom Likely cause
hangs, then times out no endpoints, NetworkPolicy, or wrong Service name resolving to nothing
"connection refused" immediately endpoints exist but wrong targetPort/app not listening
"bad address" / "could not resolve" DNS problem
works from one namespace only short name used across namespaces (web vs web.net4)
endpoints list empty, Pods Running selector mismatch or readiness failing (0/1) (Labs 7.3, 13.3)

Find the right target port without guessing: k get pod <p> -o jsonpath='{.spec.containers[*].ports}' shows only declared ports; the real listening port is in the image docs or k exec <p> -- netstat -ln (when available). Fix the Service when the task says so; do not change the Deployment.

2Readiness: Running is not Ready

A Pod with a failing readiness probe is Running but 0/1 and is removed from the Service endpoints. Look: k describe pod -> "Readiness probe failed: HTTP probe failed with statuscode: 404". Correct the probe path or port in the Deployment (Lab 13.3). Do not remove the probe if the task does not say so.

3DNS troubleshooting

k get pods -n kube-system -l k8s-app=kube-dns            # CoreDNS Pods Running and Ready?
k logs -n kube-system -l k8s-app=kube-dns --tail=20      # config errors show here
k get svc -n kube-system kube-dns                        # the DNS Service IP
k exec client -- cat /etc/resolv.conf                    # nameserver should be that IP
k exec client -- nslookup kubernetes.default.svc.cluster.local
k get cm coredns -n kube-system -o yaml                  # Corefile
Finding Cause Fix
no CoreDNS Pods Deployment scaled to 0 (Lab 8.4) k -n kube-system scale deploy coredns --replicas=2
CoreDNS CrashLoopBackOff, log "Unknown directive" typo in the Corefile (Lab 13.6) fix the ConfigMap, k -n kube-system rollout restart deploy coredns
Pod resolv.conf shows another nameserver Pod dnsPolicy: None/Default (Lab 13.5) recreate the Pod with ClusterFirst (the default)
internal names work, external names fail forward target or node DNS problem check the Corefile forward line

dnsPolicy values: ClusterFirst (default: cluster DNS first), Default (the node's resolver, no cluster names), ClusterFirstWithHostNet (for hostNetwork Pods), None (you supply dnsConfig).

4Other network faults to recognize

Symptom Check
Pods on a node cannot get IPs, node NotReady CNI Pod (k get pods -n kube-system -o wide) and /etc/cni/net.d on the node
Service works from some nodes only kube-proxy Pod on the failing node: k -n kube-system logs <kube-proxy-pod>
NodePort unreachable node IP, node port range, the Service has endpoints, a firewall/security group
Pod-to-Pod traffic blocked NetworkPolicies in the target namespace (Module 9)

5Monitoring resource usage

kubectl top shows current CPU and memory from the Metrics Server. It is a short-window snapshot, not a history.

k top nodes
k top pods -n load
k top pods -n load --sort-by=cpu              # or --sort-by=memory
k top pods -A --sort-by=memory --no-headers | head -3
k top pod duo --containers                    # per container
  • CPU is in millicores (250m = 0.25 core), memory in Mi.
  • The Metrics Server needs a minute after start before it has data; "metrics not available yet" means wait.
  • k top needs the metrics API (k get apiservice v1beta1.metrics.k8s.io) to be Available. If k top says "Metrics API not available": check the Metrics Server Pod in kube-system (k logs deploy/metrics-server -n kube-system). On clusters with self-signed kubelet certificates it needs --kubelet-insecure-tls (Lab 13.2).
  • Compare usage with requests and limits: k describe node <n> ends with "Allocated resources" (requests and limits per node), while k top node shows actual use. A Pod can be over its request and still be fine; over its memory limit it is OOM-killed (Module 11).
  • For history and alerts you would use a monitoring system such as Prometheus; the exam objective is kubectl top and reading status.

6Lab tasks

<!-- LABS: m13 -->

Lab 13.1: top pods

Domain: Troubleshooting | Points: 6 | Time: about 6 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m13-01-top-pods)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

In the namespace load, three Pods run (idle-a, idle-b and busy). Using the metrics from the Metrics Server, find the Pod that currently uses the most CPU and write only its name to ~/answers/top-pod.txt on the host.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n load top pods --sort-by=cpu
kubectl -n load top pods --sort-by=cpu --no-headers | head -1 | awk '{print $1}' > ~/answers/top-pod.txt
cat ~/answers/top-pod.txt

Lab 13.2: fix metrics server

Domain: Troubleshooting | Points: 8 | Time: about 8 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m13-02-fix-metrics-server)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

kubectl top nodes fails with an error such as "Metrics API not available". The Metrics Server runs in kube-system but is not ready. Find the cause in its logs and fix it. In this test cluster the kubelets use self-signed serving certificates, so the Metrics Server needs the argument --kubelet-insecure-tls. When done, kubectl top nodes must print the usage of all three nodes.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n kube-system get pods -l k8s-app=metrics-server
kubectl -n kube-system logs deploy/metrics-server --tail=3
kubectl -n kube-system patch deployment metrics-server --type=json -p='[{"op":"add","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/args/-","value":"--kubelet-insecure-tls"}]'
kubectl -n kube-system rollout status deployment metrics-server --timeout=120s
for i in $(seq 1 30); do kubectl top nodes >/dev/null 2>&1 && break; sleep 5; done
kubectl top nodes

Lab 13.3: readiness no endpoints

Domain: Troubleshooting | Points: 7 | Time: about 7 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m13-03-readiness-no-endpoints)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

In the namespace net3, requests to http://shop.net3 fail although the Service shop selects the right Pods. The Pods are Running but not Ready. Find the cause and fix the Deployment shop (do not change the Service) so that http://shop.net3 returns the nginx welcome page.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n net3 get pods
kubectl -n net3 describe pod -l app=shop | grep -i -A2 "Readiness probe failed" | head -4
kubectl -n net3 patch deployment shop --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/readinessProbe/httpGet/path","value":"/"}]'
kubectl -n net3 rollout status deployment shop --timeout=120s

Lab 13.4: wrong targetport

Domain: Troubleshooting | Points: 6 | Time: about 6 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m13-04-wrong-targetport)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

In the namespace net4, the Service web has endpoints, but requests to http://web.net4 end with "connection refused". The Pods are Ready and the nginx containers listen on port 80. Fix the Service (do not touch the Deployment) so that http://web.net4 works.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n net4 get endpointslices -l kubernetes.io/service-name=web -o wide
kubectl -n net4 describe svc web | grep -i -E "Port|Endpoints"
kubectl -n net4 patch svc web --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/ports/0/targetPort","value":80}]'

Lab 13.5: pod dns policy

Domain: Troubleshooting | Points: 6 | Time: about 6 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m13-05-pod-dns-policy)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

In the namespace net5, the Pod lookup cannot resolve any cluster names (for example kubernetes.default). Find the cause in the Pod spec and recreate the Pod lookup (image busybox:1.36, command sleep 3600) so that it uses the cluster DNS and can resolve kubernetes.default.svc.cluster.local.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n net5 get pod lookup -o jsonpath='{.spec.dnsPolicy}{"\n"}'
kubectl -n net5 exec lookup -- cat /etc/resolv.conf
kubectl -n net5 delete pod lookup --force --grace-period 0
kubectl -n net5 run lookup --image=busybox:1.36 --command -- sleep 3600
kubectl -n net5 wait --for=condition=Ready pod/lookup --timeout=120s
kubectl -n net5 exec lookup -- nslookup kubernetes.default.svc.cluster.local

Lab 13.6: coredns bad corefile

Domain: Troubleshooting | Points: 9 | Time: about 9 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m13-06-coredns-bad-corefile)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-cka

After a change to the CoreDNS configuration, the CoreDNS Pods in kube-system crash. Name resolution in the cluster is down. Find the error in the CoreDNS Pod logs, correct the configuration (the ConfigMap coredns), and restart CoreDNS so that 2 replicas are Ready and kubernetes.default.svc.cluster.local resolves.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n kube-system get pods -l k8s-app=kube-dns
kubectl -n kube-system logs -l k8s-app=kube-dns --tail=3
kubectl -n kube-system get configmap coredns -o jsonpath='{.data.Corefile}' | sed 's/loadbalanse/loadbalance/' > /tmp/Corefile.fixed
kubectl -n kube-system create configmap coredns --from-file=Corefile=/tmp/Corefile.fixed --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart deployment coredns
kubectl -n kube-system rollout status deployment coredns --timeout=120s

<!-- /LABS -->

7Recall questions

R1A Service times out and get endpointslices is empty. What are the two usual causes?

Show the answer

The selector does not match the Pod labels, or the Pods are not Ready (failing readiness probe).

R2Endpoints exist but the client gets "connection refused". What is wrong?

Show the answer

The Service targetPort does not match the port the container listens on.

R3What does dnsPolicy: Default do?

Show the answer

The Pod uses the node's DNS resolver, so cluster names do not resolve.

R4What do you check when nslookup fails for every cluster name?

Show the answer

The CoreDNS Pods (running and ready), their logs, and the Corefile ConfigMap.

R5Which command shows the Pod using the most CPU in a namespace?

Show the answer

kubectl top pods -n <ns> --sort-by=cpu.

R6What component does kubectl top depend on?

Show the answer

The Metrics Server (metrics API).

R7How does kubectl top node differ from the "Allocated resources" in kubectl describe node?

Show the answer

top shows actual current usage; "Allocated resources" shows the sum of requests and limits of scheduled Pods.

R8A Pod is Running but 0/1. Is it receiving Service traffic?

Show the answer

No; it is not Ready and is removed from the endpoints.

Quick Reference Card

Topic Remember
Service path DNS -> Service -> endpoints -> Pod -> port
No endpoints selector typo or readiness failing
Connection refused wrong targetPort
Timeout no endpoints or NetworkPolicy
DNS CoreDNS Pods/logs/Corefile; Pod dnsPolicy ClusterFirst
Monitoring k top nodes, k top pods --sort-by=cpu, needs Metrics Server
Requests vs use describe node (allocated) vs top (actual)
